obtained.how: the agency's own PDF of the report from the Species at Risk Public Registry (the canada.ca page cited in the entry serves the same report as HTML chapters)

bibliography.checked_against: the report's own 'may be cited as' line (PDF p. 2)
bibliography.note: 'COSEWIC 2008. COSEWIC assessment and update status report on the redbreast sunfish Lepomis auritus in Canada. Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada. Ottawa. vi + 33 pp.' As cited. The update report was written by Allen Curry and Mark Gautreau (production note), so 'Gautreau & Curry 2006, via COSEWIC 2008' relays the same authors' work. Catalogue No. CW69-14/521-2008E-PDF.

claims.claim: In Yoho and Oromocto lakes, most redbreast nests were dug through a dense plant mat to coarse sand or fine gravel (Gautreau & Curry 2006, via COSEWIC 2008)
claims.quote: The majority of the nests were excavated through a dense vegetative mat to spawning substrate
claims.conditions: 'of coarse sand to fine gravel'; nests: Yoho n = 43, Oromocto n = 20
claims.note: The same paragraph says 72 % of Yoho nests 'were associated with sparse vegetation and lacked cover structures', which sits oddly beside 'dense vegetative mat'; the paper reports only the latter.

claims.claim: In Oromocto, 85 % of nests lay within 1 m of a rock or log
claims.quote: Oromocto Lake had 85% of the nests within 1 m of a rock or log
claims.conditions: Oromocto Lake, New Brunswick, n = 20 nests; 13 cover structures at nest edges

claims.claim: Nests 51 cm across in 43 cm of water (Gautreau & Curry 2006, via COSEWIC 2008)
claims.conditions: means ± SD over Yoho (n = 43) and Oromocto (n = 20) nests; 'were in water depths of 43.2 ± 8.4 cm'; excavated 7.1 ± 2.5 cm deep
claims.note: Range-wide (Scott & Crossman 1998, same page): nests 61–102 cm across in 15–40 cm of water.

claims.claim: Spawning late June–early July as water nears 20 °C in New Brunswick (Gautreau & Curry 2006, via COSEWIC 2008)
claims.quote: from late June to early July when the water temperature approached 20oC
claims.conditions: Yoho and Oromocto lakes; range-wide peak at 16.7–27.8 °C (Scott & Crossman 1998)
claims.note: The source says 'water temperature', not 'littoral' water (Table 3.5-2's wording).

claims.claim: Fecundity 963–8,250 at 139–235 mm (North Carolina); 1,396–4,138 at 100–175 mm (Florida) (southern, via COSEWIC 2008)
claims.quote: 963 – 8250 eggs for fish 139 – 235 mm in total length
claims.conditions: two south-eastern North Carolina rivers (Davis 1972); Santa Fe River, Florida: '1396 – 4138 eggs for redbreast sunfish having total lengths of 100 – 175 mm' (Bass & Hitt 1974); total length

claims.claim: Male care; larvae 1–2 weeks in the nest
claims.source_value: Values right, attribution not: in COSEWIC the male care is from Lukas & Orth 1993 and Scott & Crossman 1998, and the 1–2 weeks in the nest from DeWoody et al. 1998, not from Gautreau & Curry 2006, whom the row credits for everything (via COSEWIC).
claims.quote: Larval redbreast sunfish remain in the nest for one to two weeks before dispersing
claims.conditions: the male 'begins to defend and aerate the eggs' (Lukas & Orth 1993; Scott & Crossman 1998); the 1–2 weeks is DeWoody et al. 1998
claims.note: Cite as 'DeWoody et al. 1998, via COSEWIC 2008'. Hatch length: COSEWIC gives a mean of 4.9 mm TL (Buynak & Mohr 1978), within the row's 4.6–5.1 mm.

claims.claim: Redbreast aggregate in deeper water below 5 °C (Breder & Nigrelli 1935, via COSEWIC 2008)
claims.quote: aggregate in deeper waters to overwinter when water temperature falls below 5ºC
claims.conditions: credited to Breder & Nigrelli 1935 and Scott & Crossman 1998; the summary (PDF p. 4) adds they 'remain inactive under the ice until spring'

claims.claim: Two-thirds of tagged redbreast in a Tennessee stream moved less than 100 m, a few 4–9 km (Gatz & Adams 1994, via COSEWIC 2008)
claims.quote: two thirds of all fish moving less than 100 metres
claims.conditions: individually tagged fish over three years; 'The greatest movement (4 – 9 km) was by a few individuals', later recaptured near their tagging sites; Gatz & Adams's title: 'two warmwater streams in eastern Tennessee'

claims.claim: Yoho Lake young-of-year 36.2 mm at the end of the first season (back-calculated; Gautreau & Curry 2006 via COSEWIC 2008)
claims.conditions: direct proportional back-calculation from scales of 27 Yoho Lake fish, 2005; 'average total lengths for 0+ through 5+ fish' at the end of the growing season
claims.note: These are also the 36, 64, 88, 111, 127, 141 mm that Table 3.5-2 credits to Gautreau & Curry 2012.

tried.note: ECONNRESET (the same file was served from sararegistry.gc.ca without www)

notes: Other values here the paper uses under other citations: Carlander (1977) 'reach maturity at a weight of 23 g or in their second year' (PDF p. 23; the paper's Table 3.5-2 credits Carlander 1977 directly, the references say via COSEWIC); individuals to age 8 (Carlander 1977); Yoho fish 126 ± 26 mm TL and 42.4 ± 24.8 g, Oromocto 143 ± 33 mm and 80.9 ± 52.5 g (Gautreau & Curry 2006; Table 3.5-2's 12.5 cm and 42.6 g are credited to Gautreau & Curry 2012 and differ slightly); guarding males 16.6 and 15.7 cm fork length (2005, 2006); Yoho population estimate 810 ± 115 (2005). Full citation of the relayed report: Gautreau, M. & Curry, R. A. 2006. Ecology of the redbreast sunfish, Lepomis auritus, in Yoho and Oromocto Lakes. NB Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research Unit Report 01-06, 17 p.
